text:
julia: Heads-up — local sample app fails on Vercel Edge when running with pnpm workspace symlinks enabled. Error: 'Unexpected token' while importing our JS SDK. Anyone seen this? I can repro with latest main.

sam: Error/logs? paste the stack?

julia: gist: `https://gist.github.com/...` main part: `SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export' at runtime` when edge runtime loads node-style cjs entrypoint.

kevin: Likely exports resolution + CJS/ESM mismatch. Edge runtimes require ESM; if the package.json exports default to CJS or the consumer ends up resolving the cjs path, you'll see that. Check package.json exports + the published layout.

maria: can you paste the package.json from the SDK package? specifically exports/types field

julia: here's what we had in the monorepo (simplified):
```json
{
  "name": "@redwood/sdk",
  "version": "0.0.0",
  "main": "dist/cjs/index.cjs",
  "types": "dist/cjs/index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    "./package.json": "./package.json"
  }
}
```

kevin: ah — that explains it. main points: 1) main points to CJS; 2) exports doesn't provide an import entry for ESM so bundlers/runtime end up using CJS. Edge will choke. Also note: some bundlers won't be able to read types unless you map them in exports or put a top-level types that points at ESM types.

alex: another pnpm-specific gotcha: workspace symlinks mean the app resolves the package from the FS location and some bundlers (vite/rollup) can follow realpaths and treat the package differently. Also Node's resolver and package exports can hide subpaths — if your consumer tries to import `@redwood/sdk/dist/esm` it may be rejected because exports doesn't allow that subpath. Two options: expose an explicit ESM import via exports, or provide a dedicated `/edge` subpath.

kevin: recommended exports shape for multi-targets:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"
  },
  "./edge": {
    "import": "./dist/edge/index.mjs"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
That gives consumers an explicit ESM import and an opt-in edge entrypoint. Also add a top-level `types": "dist/esm/index.d.ts"` (or include types under the export map) so TS picks it up for ESM imports.

maria: fyi TS behavior: TypeScript will read the `types` or `typings` at the package root regardless of exports, but if you want path-specific types use the `types` field or `"exports" -> "types"` (supported in newer TS). To be conservative add a root `types` field pointing to the ESM d.ts.

julia: I tried the exports change locally (add import/require plus ./edge). Rebuilt, linked, deployed the example app to Vercel preview -> Edge runtime now accepts the import and app runs.

sam: nice. Can we also add a short troubleshooting blurb for devs using pnpm workspaces? e.g. mention `node --preserve-symlinks` and the vite `server.fs.strict` and `optimizeDeps.exclude/include` bits?

alex: yeah: dev notes: 1) if you see different resolution locally vs prod with pnpm, try `--preserve-symlinks` to force runtime to treat packages like installed ones; 2) for Vite in workspace, add the package to optimizeDeps.include if prebundling fails; 3) prefer explicit exports instead of relying on subpath imports.

maria: also add test in examples/edge-app that imports `@redwood/sdk/edge` under a pnpm workspace setup so CI can catch regressions.

julia: will open PR with: exports map (import/require + ./edge), top-level types -> dist/esm/index.d.ts, add ./package.json export, and an example test that runs the example edge app in workspace mode.

deploy-bot: CI build started for branch/exports-fix (job #4821)

sam: thanks — can you also add a brief note in the DX guide about "how to import for edge vs node" and a snippet showing `import sdk from '@redwood/sdk/edge'`? makes onboarding smoother.

julia: adding that to README and the onboarding checklist. PR coming in ~30m.

deploy-bot: CI passed for branch/exports-fix — all checks green :tada:

kevin: great work. follow-up idea: add a small script `scripts/check-exports.js` to validate that package exports cover import/require/types/./package.json in CI. prevents accidental regressions.

julia: done in PR — added check + test + README update. Thanks everyone :pray:
